sentences.text:
In short the prosecution case is that the prosecutrix and her mother lodged an oral report in P.S.
Bichhiya that on 10.3.2024 at about 3:00 PM while the prosecutrix was filling water from the handpump then the appellant - Virendra Saket and co- accused Shani Saket (absconding) came and gaged her mouth and made her to sit in the motorcycle and took her towards the river and raped her in a deserted field and threatened her that if she discloses the incident to anyone then they would kill her.

On reaching home, the prosecutrix narrated the incident to her mother and thereafter report of the incident (Ex.P-1) was lodged as Crime No.88/2024.
3.
During course of investigation the accused was arrested and was medically examined.
The statements of witnesses were recorded.
Vaginal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49914 3 CRA-7212-2025 slides of the prosecutrix were prepared.
On the basis of memorandum (Ex.P- 17) the motorcycle bearing No.M.P.-12-MQ-2254 was seized by seizure memo Ex.P-7.
Blood sample of the accused was sent for chemical examination analysis.
DNA (Ex.P-20) was received and charge -sheet was filed against the appellant.
4. When the charges were levelled for the offence as mentioned above, the appellant denied the same.
After prosecution evidence when he was examined under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. the appellant denied the prosecution evidence and pleaded himself to be innocent and had given the defence evidence.
5. Against conviction and sentence the appeal has been filed on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
There is delay in lodging the FIR.
There is no medical evidence to corroborate the assault or rape.
Test Identification Parade was not conducted.
FIR does not show that features of the persons who took away the prosecutrix was mentioned, hence prayer is made for acquittal of the appellant from the charges by allowing this appeal.
6. On the other hand, Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Government Advocate for the State submits that judgment of the trial court is well justified.
No ground for interference in conviction and sentence of the appellant is made out, hence the appeal be dismissed.

sentences.text: 7. PW-1 has stated that she knows the appellant and another absconding co-accused - Shani Shaket as they are resident of same locality.
Her date of birth is 28th November 2007.
She has studied upto 10 th Class.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49914 4 CRA-7212-2025 8. PW-2
mother of the prosecutrix has stated that prosecutrix is 17 years of age.
In cross-examination, she has stated that she has four daughters and a son.
Prosecutrix is her youngest daughter.
In para-4 of cross - examination she has stated that when she went to get the prosecutrix admitted in the school, then she got her date of birth recorded in the school by estimation.
She further admitted that when prosecutrix was admitted in the school, at that time she was about 7-8 years of age.
She further stated that the prosecutrix was 6 years of age.
She admitted that the birth certificate of the prosecutrix was not prepared.
9. PW-3 Sandeep Kumar Bhalla Head Master of the school stated that as per school record date of birth of the prosecutrix is 28.11.2007.
The prosecutrix took admission in 1st Class on 3.7.2013.
Mother of the prosecutrix had given an Aganwadi Certificate.
In para-2 of cross- examination this witness admitted that at the time of admission the parents of the prosecutrix did not bring any birth certificate.
10. PW-4 Dr. Priti Mishra has stated that the mother of the prosecutrix had not given any birth proof therefore, she had advised for Dental X-ray and X-ray of bone to determine her age.

11. Therefore although 10 th Class mark-sheet (Ex.P-5-C) is available on record which mentions the date of birth as 28.11.2007 of the prosecutrix but at the time of admission when evidence of date of birth as to whether any reliable oral or documentary evidence is available on record is seen, we find that inspite of advise/direction of the PW-4 Dr. Priti Mishra, Dental and Bone X-ray of the prosecutrix was not done to determine her age.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49914 5 CRA-7212-2025 12.

In the scholar register (Ex.P-9-C) and Aganwadi Certificate (PW- 10) (which is not a recognized document of age) as per Section 94 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 the date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 28.11.2007 but when PW-4 Dr. Priti Mishra in medical examination has specially directed for X-ray of bone and dental to determine her age, then in not producing the x-ray reports would weaken the prosecution case regarding age of prosecutrix.

sentences.text: On this point the relevant judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana report in (2010) 1 SCC 742 is relevant wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that when prosecution has failed to prove the age of the prosecutrix on the date of incident and with other relevant facts, and when tests regarding age as advised by Doctor were not conducted, then it is a serious flaw in prosecution case and accordingly the benefit of doubt was given to the accused.

sentences.text: Dr. Verma, PW 1, who had clinically examined the prosecutrix, found that her secondary sex characters were well developed.
The short question in the facts and circumstances of this case that remains to be determined is whether the prosecutrix was a minor?
Dr. Sadhna Verma, PW 1 who examined the prosecutrix referred her for verification to the dental surgeon and the radiologist.

The failure of getting the prosecutrix examined from the dental surgeon or the radiologist despite the fact that she was referred to them by Dr. Sadhna Verma, PW 1 is a serious flaw in the prosecution version.

We are not laying down as a rule that all these tests must be performed in all cases, but in the instant case, in the absence of primary evidence,
reports of the dental surgeon and the radiologist would have helped us in arriving at the conclusion regarding the age of the prosecutrix.
13.

Therefore in the light of the oral and documentary evidence and in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:49914 6 CRA-7212-2025 the light of judgment of Sunil (supra), we hold that finding of learned trial court in Para-14 of the judgment that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age and was of the age of 16 years, 3 months and 10 days cannot be upheld.

Accordingly, we set aside this finding and hold that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of incident and the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age.
14.

Once we hold that on the date of offence the prosecutrix was not minor being less than 18 years of age, then conviction under Section 5(g)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 cannot be sustained and accordingly the appellant is acquitted from the charge of Section 5(g)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012.

Regarding conviction under the other Sections, reading from statements of PW-1 wherein she has narrated that in the incident present appellant and another absconded co- accused forcefully made her to sit on a motorcycle and took her to deserted field near river and raped her is very crucial.
PW-2 mother of the prosecutrix has also supported the story narrated by the prosecutrix to her.

16. PW-14 Dr. Priti Mishra has stated that although there was no pain or injury or marks therefore,
she cannot say that prosecutrix was raped but there is DNA report (Ex.P-20) which shows that DNA obtained from the blood sample of the appellant were found on the vaginal slide of the DNA of prosecutrix which confirms the offence of rape, abduction to commit gang rape and threat, and on careful reading of the cross-examination of the prosecutrix it is seen that nothing has come in the cross - examination on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49914 7 CRA-7212-2025 basis of which appellant can be acquitted from the remaining Sections under which he has been convicted by the learned trial court.
17.
